# Critic panel sheet

Read-only. Nothing applied. Pick by critic and number.

## Diagnoses

**levine:** Yes, it is past fine: the plumber's second truck, "That number is the price of laptops," the henhouse sections shipping assembled, and the fourth check applied to a Forbes vice president are all sentences a reader will repeat to someone else, which is the only test that matters. What holds it back is a reflex that shows up maybe a dozen times — the draft lands a dry fact, then adds a following clause that tells the reader what the fact just did, and the clause spends the laugh the fact had already earned. The related tic is the hedge in front position ("For the most part," "In most cases," "may claim"), which apologizes for a flat sentence before the sentence gets to be flat.

**didion:** It is past fine in its exhibits and still merely fine in its connective prose: the deck, the henhouse, the laptop, the plumber's form, the one chair the consequences cannot reach — those hold, and nothing needs adding to them. What holds the piece back now is the sentence that follows the object and restates it in the register the essay is prosecuting, most damagingly in the risk paragraph, which shifts a hazard onto "whoever executes" while the surrounding pages are convicting other writers for exactly that dodge. A smaller symptom of the same slackness: "the oldest in business" at the third question and "the oldest move in business" nine paragraphs later, a formula the piece spends twice and earns once.

**hemingway:** It is more than fine in four places — the plumber and his second truck, the pods sentence, the fourth check run on the Forbes post, and the two Duolingo performances staged by one company in one year — and merely fine in the connective stretches between them. Further clause-cutting would now chop: the sentences are at working weight, and shaving inside them would cost the plainness the specimens depend on for contrast. What still cuts clean is the whole restated sentence, because the piece states its thesis five times in different clothing, and every suggestion below removes a restatement rather than a clause.

## Convergent (2 sentences targeted by 2+ critics)

### "Ten years have found me responsible for AI strategy in production systems, which mostly means I am the one who must state what a plan will cost and who will actually pay for it, and I write every article with AI assistance, spending hours each week extracting prose that looks finished from these models."

- **levine:** Ten years have found me responsible for AI strategy in production systems, which mostly means I am the one who states what a plan will cost and who pays for it. I also write every article with AI assistance, spending hours each week extracting prose that looks finished from these models. — *Fifty words carrying two separate credentials become two sentences, so the second admission is heard instead of trailing the first.*
- **didion:** For ten years I have been responsible for AI strategy in production systems, which mostly means I am the one who has to say what a plan will cost and who will pay for it. I also draft every article with these models, hours a week spent pulling prose that looks finished out of them. — *Two receipts stop competing inside one 60-word sentence, and "Ten years have found me" stops sounding like a memoir opening.*

### "Trying to size a business that does not exist reveals nothing about whether it will ever exist."

- **didion:** CUT — *The sentence circles back on its own terms; the money-moving-past line before it has already landed and is weakened by the follow-up.*
- **hemingway:** CUT — *The fifth sentence of a five-sentence paragraph that has already made the point twice in better metaphors. The paragraph ends on the world/we contrast instead of trailing into abstraction.*

## Single-critic suggestions

### levine

1. "For the most part, the companies making money from AI were not the companies making announcements about it." → The companies making money from AI were not the companies making announcements about it. — *The section's opening line stops apologizing for itself three words before it lands.*
2. "Those nouns can be swapped, as the noun does no actual work." → CUT — *The swap test in the next sentence is the joke; stating the verdict first pays it out before the reader can.*
3. "If these ideas are so easily debunked, why do so many of them survive contact with senior management?" → The ideas are easy to debunk. They survive senior management anyway. — *Removes a one-line question paragraph — the piece's most generic move — and the answers that follow arrive as answers rather than as a quiz key.*
4. "CTO Andrew Bosworth answered that the time should actually serve the users and publicly questioned the employee's approach to their career in front of the entire gathering, later calling his remark humorous [23]." → CTO Andrew Bosworth answered that the time should serve the users, then questioned the employee's approach to their career in front of the whole Q&A. He later called the remark humorous [23]. — *Cuts the redundancy of "publicly... in front of the entire gathering" and moves the best fact in the anecdote to end position, where it works unassisted.*
5. "A slide may claim an opportunity runs into the trillions, but whose revenue does that number actually describe? In most cases the answer is nobody's." → A slide claims the opportunity runs into the trillions. The trillions are nobody's revenue. — *Two flat statements instead of a hedged question and its own answer; the sentence after it already supplies the proof, so the question was doing no work.*

### didion

1. "I have not met the man, and a picture of him is not the same as a man understood." → I have not met the man, and this picture of him is a guess. — *Removes an aphorism-shaped clause from the last position before the locked close, and fixes the pronoun, which currently refers to a picture rather than to the guess.*
2. "Theater remains, because a chatbot and the right vocabulary keep up appearances." → Theater remains, because a chatbot and the right vocabulary cost less than the people who could answer the questions. — *Ends the section on the trade the restructuring actually made instead of a stock phrase, and closes the loop with the expensive seniors two sentences earlier.*
3. "A document that raises the risk and names no mitigation does not remove the risk; it merely shifts it onto whoever executes." → A document that raises the risk and names no mitigation does not remove the risk; it hands the risk to the people who will be in the room when the number does not arrive. — *Puts bodies where the sentence currently has a passive shadow, and stops the essay from committing the agentless dodge it catalogues.*
4. "The difference between a real strategy and a document that looks like one depends on three questions: what are we building, who is going to buy it, and how much money are we going to make." → Three questions separate a strategy from a document that looks like one: what are we building, who is going to buy it, and how much money are we going to make. — *Drops a banned intensifier and a limp verb; the questions do the separating instead of a difference depending on them.*

### hemingway

1. "A text can be long and well-researched and still say nothing checkable about what ships." → CUT — *The Block paragraph closes three times; this is the abstract one, and the two survivors ("It is the pods sentence, grown to 3,000 words" and "longest exactly where it is emptiest") land harder alone.*
2. "That is the problem in one experiment." → CUT — *A label for the paragraph that follows it, arriving one line after the locked "758 of them, with controls" close. Cutting it lets the strongest sentence in the section stand undisturbed.*
3. "An argument makes a claim that could be wrong." → CUT — *Starts the paragraph on the concrete sentence ("You take a stand and admit that a fact might undermine you") instead of restating it in the abstract first.*
4. "That coherence feels like validation, yet the model gave form, not evidence." → The model gave form, not evidence. — *Removes the second "validation" three sentences after the first, and drops the hinge so the sentence hits on the beat the short ones before it set up.*
5. "One instance might reflect a bad day or a poorly phrased question, while a second occurrence signals a pattern, not a coincidence." → One instance might reflect a bad day or a poorly phrased question. — *The clause removed only restates "ask twice" from the sentence before it. The reader already did that arithmetic.*

## Paragraph-level moves

**levine:** Move the "Ask twice, in two different meetings" paragraph up so it sits directly after "These are ordinary questions asked in good faith to be helpful," before the Bosworth anecdote. As written it is procedural advice placed after the section's payoff, so the closing beat of the whole argument is a caveat about bad days and poorly phrased questions rather than "before the year you would have spent executing it." Relocated, it reads as part of the instruction for how to ask, and the Bosworth receipt plus the price-of-one-question line close the section on its strongest two sentences and hand off cleanly to the locked ending.

**didion:** Move the three-sentence paragraph beginning "An argument makes a claim that could be wrong" up to sit immediately after the Figure 1 caption, where the picture has just shown a sentence that can be proven wrong beside one that cannot. The definition currently arrives eighteen paragraphs late, as abstraction the figure already made visible; placed against the figure it reads as a caption to an object, and its departure lets the alibi paragraph run straight into Orwell's henhouse.

**hemingway:** Move the credential paragraph ("Ten years have found me responsible for AI strategy in production systems…") out of "Why the Machine Is Good at This" and up to sit immediately after the specimen-generation paragraph ("These examples were not from a presentation… The exhibits below are what prove it is in use"). Two things happen. The receipt lands where it is load-bearing: the claim that a finished look proves nothing is the claim the eight fabricated specimens just demonstrated, and the admission of drafting with these tools belongs beside the sentence describing how the specimens were made, not eight sections later. And the machine section then runs uninterrupted from the chatbot's three pillars straight into the BCG experiment, which is one argument in two paragraphs and currently has a bio wedged between them.
